title: Boundary realization after the finite-Tor comparison step
statement: Fix a finite-field datum, a prime $\ell$ different from its characteristic, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type schemes over this field. Use the four published finite-Tor constructible predicates [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] and the exact canonical functors and dualizing objects in the finite-site data [def-weil-boundary-finite-site-data]. Assume EtaleHypotheses at this datum. Then BasicRemainder and EvaluationAt hold. BasicRemainder asserts bounded-below Hom bijectivity, Noetherianity, a natural-number dimension bound, direct-image mate invertibility, and the specified counit/projection comparisons with invertible components. EvaluationAt is the original canonical EvaluationConclusion: the dualizing objects belong to their four predicates; the specified inverse images, exceptional images and duals preserve them; the canonical origin, evaluation and dualizing-composition comparisons have their prescribed normalizations; a natural pro-etale q family agrees on etale representatives with the ordinary-counit Hom transpose; and the literal evaluation-defined alpha and beta have the displayed comparison squares and transport the boundary composite identity and invertibility, including all pro-etale finite-Tor inputs. This statement omits the two finite-Tor subcategory equivalences, both Tor-interval comparison clauses and both etale-representative clauses, which are proved separately.

proof.text: Apply the existing boundary projection comparison for the Hom, mate, counit and projection clauses. The assumed exceptional preservation supplies constructibility. Boundary etale adjunction restriction evaluated at the identity-open proper compactification supplies Noetherianity and finite dimension. Finite proper projection makes the etale projection invertible; the inverse comparison square makes its pro-etale component invertible. Use the proved finite-Tor comparison separately for both schemes to supply the representatives needed below.

Use the invertible comparison unit on D+ for the canonical exceptional-origin isomorphism, and the pullback square for inverse-image comparison. Etale representatives in BasicConclusion and the assumed etale preservation transfer both preservation assertions to the actual pro-etale functors.

The finite coefficient unit has Tor interval [0,0]. Closed monoidal unitors identify its dual with omega_T, so assumed dual preservation gives omega_T and assumed exceptional preservation gives G omega_T. The canonical dualizing composition compares this to the specified omega_Z,p with its pasted-counit normalization.

Apply finite-duality site comparison to these dualizing objects and all restrictions and iterated duals. It supplies evaluation-normalized chi, the normalized ambient duality pairings, and double-dual compatibility. Transfer preservation of duals along the supplied etale representatives.

Transpose inverse projection followed by the normalized exceptional counit through the supplied bijective Hom transport to construct q on representatives. Naturality of each factor and full faithfulness descend it to all finite-Tor objects. Boundary q compatibility identifies it with assembleProQ and comparedEtaleQ. The finite compact-support projection formula and representative transport make the required pro-etale projection components invertible.

Transpose the q/evaluation identities through tensor-Hom to get the alpha and beta squares in their displayed factor order. Apply comparison to CompositeIdentity, substitute double-dual and transpose compatibility, and cancel comparison isomorphisms. Conjugate images of inverse maps for invertibility; naturality and the supplied etale representatives extend it to all inputs.
